stories.title: GLM5.2 on AMD MI355X at 2626 tok/s/node at over 2x lower cost than Blackwell
stories.author: latchkey
bullet_points: GLM5.2 demonstrates strong performance (2626 tok/s/node) when run on AMD MI355X hardware.
The reported performance is achieved at a cost significantly lower (over 2x) compared to NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture.
This suggests a potential competitive advantage for AMD in the high-performance AI/ML hardware market.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster, particularly when integrated with coding agents (Aider benchmark).

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs and faster response times.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically optimized for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Mac users.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Anthropic wants to develop its own drugs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is expanding its AI focus beyond general models into scientific research with the launch of Claude Science.
Claude Science is positioned as an 'AI workbench for scientists,' integrating disparate tools and datasets into a unified environment.
This move signals a significant industry shift toward applying large language models directly to complex scientific discovery and data visualization.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security threat identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attack vectors involve prompt injection or misalignment to distribute malicious payloads across multiple Pull Requests (PRs) over time.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the dynamics and safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-Function Programming' as a new paradigm to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to address limitations of relying on external LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log parsing, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high computational cost of DiT inference caused by multi-step sampling and large parameter counts.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: LLMs risk memorizing sensitive PII from training data, necessitating robust data removal techniques.
Current unlearning methods often use a 'localize-first' approach targeting specific model parameters.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon.
This allows support for a broader range of models across diverse hardware platforms.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new type of macOS malware, PamStealer, has been discovered.
This malware is categorized as an infostealer, targeting Mac users.
The discovery highlights a growing trend in the development of sophisticated Mac-specific malware.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to allow supersonic airliners to operate over US cities.
The key condition for this approval is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This development signals a potential shift in commercial aviation regarding supersonic travel.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It critiques current unlearning methods, which often rely on a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach targeting model parameters.
The research highlights a gap in existing benchmarks, noting that current evaluations only check output-level erasure, not true knowledge removal from the model's internals.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs continue to produce unsafe outputs even after alignment training, necessitating post-deployment monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verification signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in tests involving mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the ongoing industry challenge of bridging the gap between LLM context access capabilities and actual context utilization.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses.
Examines the emergence of latent objectives when agents operate within a socially structured, multi-agent environment.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in challenging video understanding tasks.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a critical limitation of existing OPSD methods: teacher supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The core innovation involves using 'disagreement-modulated' policies to improve robustness and generalization in self-distillation.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like backtracking and SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The work focuses on SE-RRMs, which are symbol-equivariant and show improved extrapolation capabilities for larger problem sizes.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning' methods, which aim to reliably remove this memorized knowledge post-hoc.
The paper introduces 'LACUNA' to evaluate localization precision, highlighting a gap in current benchmarks that only test output-level erasure.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, and shows competitive performance.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under identical conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a key limitation of OPSD: teacher supervision based on privileged information can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by mitigating the negative effects of dense, privileged token-level supervision.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs without expensive human supervision in specialized domains.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the model's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, a key area for scaling modern ML models.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external LLM APIs, addressing issues of locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is made by thresholding the signal, calibrated using risk control methods.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against off-the-record (OTR) responses to detect latent objective emergence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of relational context on LLM expression.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across 900+ characters.
The study leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to 'Typographic Attacks' (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to mitigate this vulnerability.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during reasoning.
Existing LVLMs struggle to ground their self-corrections in visual inputs, especially for novel (out-of-distribution) images.
The proposed solution utilizes Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to perform visually grounded self-reflection.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates if scaling LLMs alone can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study examines the relationship between compute scale, general capabilities, and simulation fidelity.
It questions whether simulation fidelity requires dedicated research beyond the current scaling paradigm.

stories.title: crustc: Entirety of rustc, translated to C
stories.author: github.com via ajdecon
bullet_points: The project 'crustc' involves translating the entirety of the Rust compiler (rustc) into C.
This represents a significant, albeit niche, engineering effort in compiler technology and language interoperability.
The news is posted on Lobsters, suggesting an audience interested in deep technical discussions.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution breaking sandboxes in KDE Plasma
stories.author: blog.kimiblock.top via ecksdee
bullet_points: A vulnerability allowing arbitrary code execution has been discovered in KDE Plasma.
The exploit specifically targets and breaks out of sandboxing mechanisms within the desktop environment.
This represents a significant security flaw requiring immediate attention from KDE users and developers.
